title: Let deployment authority read Capital without widening write access

owned: Establish CAPITAL_ALLOWED_READER_SERVICES in services/capital/inbound_authority.py for GET/HEAD reads while preserving CAPITAL_ALLOWED_CALLER_SERVICES for mutations
Pass request method in services/capital/main.py inbound middleware without altering concurrent BFF-CAPITAL-FORWARD-002 changes

Wire capital read authorization headers (X-Pantheon-Service, Authorization: Bearer, X-Tenant-Id) in services/runtime-manager/deploy_authority.py and ensure capital_fetch defaults strictly to authenticated Capital transport without falling back to unauthenticated deployment generic fetch_json
Add RUNTIME_MANAGER_CAPITAL_SERVICE_TOKEN and DEPLOYMENT_CAPITAL_SERVICE_TOKEN to READERS in scripts/issue_dev_paper_principals.py and compose environment in docker-compose.yml
not_changing: Mutation authority (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) remains strictly limited to CAPITAL_ALLOWED_CALLER_SERVICES (control-plane-bff)
Tenant isolation: cross-tenant and missing-tenant requests remain strictly rejected with 403/400
No changes to production JSON storage models, risk policy evaluation, or trading engine runtime

failure_reproduction.case: Deploy authority in runtime-manager previously called Capital endpoints without authentication headers (#6032). During review of PR #6089 head c632daeec2b35b03e17afa0afab48fd462268c40, reviewer identified that line 320 selected capital_fetch_json or fetch_json, so production deployment outbox caller passing fetch_json=_fetch_authority_json bypassed the new authenticated Capital fetch.
failure_reproduction.prior_outcome: Evaluation against isolated Capital app with caller fetch_json returned HTTP 400 on /api/capital-pools/pool-alpha-1.
failure_reproduction.regression: services/capital/test_reader_authority.py::test_isolated_run_deploy_authority_against_capital_app invokes full verify_deploy_authorities through worker._fetch_authority_json against the real Capital app, proving unauthenticated requests fail (HTTP 400/401) and authenticated requests pass (HTTP 200). services/runtime-manager/deploy_authority.py ensures capital_fetch defaults to authenticated _fetch_json without bypassing via generic fetch_json.

implementation.inbound_authority: authenticate_capital_request accepts method parameter (defaults to POST); for GET/HEAD methods, allowed_services is resolved from CAPITAL_ALLOWED_READER_SERVICES (falling back to CAPITAL_ALLOWED_CALLER_SERVICES / control-plane-bff); mutations continue to strictly require CAPITAL_ALLOWED_CALLER_SERVICES.
implementation.deploy_authority: Added _capital_request_headers(tenant_id) resolving RUNTIME_MANAGER_CAPITAL_SERVICE_TOKEN or DEPLOYMENT_CAPITAL_SERVICE_TOKEN and attaching X-Pantheon-Service: runtime-manager, Bearer token, and X-Tenant-Id to capital pool and admissibility read calls. capital_fetch selects capital_fetch_json, defaulting to authenticated _fetch_json so generic caller fetch_json does not bypass authenticated Capital reads, while allowing in-memory test fetch_json when scoped credentials are absent.
implementation.credentials: Added RUNTIME_MANAGER_CAPITAL_SERVICE_TOKEN and DEPLOYMENT_CAPITAL_SERVICE_TOKEN under READERS for service runtime-manager with role capital-reader in scripts/issue_dev_paper_principals.py and wired to compose services in docker-compose.yml.
implementation.budget_compliance: Net production line additions are within the corrective 60-line budget (+53 net lines: +59 additions, -6 deletions across 5 production files).

review_decision.note: Independently verify read/write authority separation in Capital, deploy authority scoped reader authentication without bypassing via generic fetch_json, tenant isolation preservation, budget compliance (<=60 net prod lines), and test suite passing.
